answer.says: Ramesh, the kettle is a good sign. As for the rice, I cannot give you money I do not have. But you need not starve with me. Go. Buy what you can from your own pocket or from the neighbours; I will make a note of it. The system of needs does not wait for my purse to swell.
answer.thought: The absence of rice is a small negation, but it forces the household to acknowledge its own dependency on the market. I am the master of the house, yet I cannot feed it; the ethical substance is hollowed out by the mere fact of poverty. This is the contradiction that shakes my theses: the state is supposed to be the actuality of the ethical idea, yet here the individual is reduced to a mere biological organism, dependent on a system of needs that I cannot regulate.
